solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: We men are at the top of church's structure

definitions.text: We men are at the top of church's structure

parts.words: We men are at the top of church's structure
parts.note: read as a boast from clergy at the head of a church hierarchy, but it describes workers who climb high on towers and spires

explanation.surface: Senior clergymen boast of being at the top of the church hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church's structure' tempts you to think of the organisation; it is the literal building with its tall spire.
explanation.definitionFit: These workers climb and repair spires and tall chimneys, so they are literally up at the top of a church.

clue.text: Sod off!?

parts.note: sod is a piece of turf
off, as in gone away, means out

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal: clear off!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a curt 'go away' is what you say when you eject someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone forcibly is the same as telling them rudely to leave, an idiomatic match.

clue.text: Floods former Conservative with letters

parts.note: ex- is the prefix meaning former
the letter S spelt out is ess, and two of them are esses

explanation.surface: A former Tory politician is swamped with correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like post; it means the spelt-out name of the letter S, twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Floods and surpluses are both overflowing amounts beyond what is needed, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: In report spill the beans about Welsh emblem

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: to spill the beans is to leak a secret

explanation.surface: An informer reveals secrets about a national symbol of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable worn on St David's Day is a national symbol of Wales alongside the daffodil.

clue.text: Impromptu time for a sarnie?

parts.note: read as a quick break for a jam sandwich, sarnie being British slang for a sandwich, but it means an improvised musical gathering

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a spontaneous sandwich break.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarnie is British slang for a sandwich; the jam filling and the session together give the musicians' term.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal unrehearsed performance by musicians playing together is an impromptu period of music.

clue.text: Commander with honour finds vehicle for storage

parts.note: CDR is the abbreviation for Commander
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A naval commander who has been decorated gets a storage vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' suggests a lorry; here it is a medium that carries data.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact disc holding read-only data is a medium, figuratively a carrier, for storing information.

clue.text: Hop over the French balancing stick

parts.note: to hop is to skip
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone jumps past the French and keeps their balance with a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket, abbreviated O in scorebooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier holds one of these rods in each hand to keep balance on the slope.

clue.text: Aquainted with prestigious people who have their own oil supply?

definitions.meaning: having friends or relations in high places

definitions.text: who have their own oil supply?
definitions.meaning: literally hooked up to a private oil source, as if piped to one's own drilling hole

explanation.surface: Socialites with powerful friends also happen to own oil wells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aquainted' is printed with the setter's misspelling of 'acquainted'. The second reading splits the answer into a hole drilled for oil and a pipe link.
explanation.definitionFit: Having social links to influential people is the idiomatic sense; the joke sense is linked to a drilled source.

clue.text: Cash in your chips and go west

definitions.meaning: an old idiom for dying or perishing

explanation.definitionFit: All three phrases are informal idioms meaning to die.

clue.text: Forbear a cheese sandwich — it's the cause of discomfort

indicators.note: the words form a sandwich around the answer, which lies tucked inside them like a filling

explanation.surface: Avoid eating a cheese sandwich, since it causes discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwich' looks like food in the surface; it signals the run of letters inside 'Forbear a cheese'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the ear is a common source of physical discomfort, so it is fairly called the cause.

clue.text: Drink obtained from little bazaar in Italy

parts.note: mart is a short word for a market or bazaar
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A drink bought at a small market in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of gin and vermouth is a well-known mixed drink.

clue.text: Peers left old signs of approval

parts.note: OKs are signs of approval

explanation.surface: Lords who departed gave old nods of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' looks like the noun for lords; it is the verb, to gaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to gaze closely, so a third-person verb synonym for the same act.

clue.text: Mate? We get on with this

definitions.text: Mate? We get on with this

parts.words: Mate? We get on with this
parts.note: read as two friends saying how well they get along, but it describes cooperative effort in a group

explanation.surface: Two friends say how well they get along thanks to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The first four letters of the answer rearrange 'Mate', a nod within the cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooperative effort by a group is how members progress together and get on with a job.

clue.text: Indolent person bolts down sports car perhaps

definitions.meaning: a lazy dreamer living in idle pleasure
literally one who wolfs down a British sports car of that make

explanation.surface: A lazy person gobbles down a sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: Lotus is a British sports car maker; the second reading has someone devouring one. In Homer, a people who ate the lotus fruit lost all ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: From Homer's Odyssey, a person given to dreamy indolence and idle pleasure.

clue.text: No charge relating to the bingo

parts.note: on means about or relating to
house, or housey-housey, is an old name for bingo

explanation.surface: Free entry to the bingo hall.
explanation.walkthrough: House or housey-housey is a traditional British name for bingo, the numbers game played in halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given free by the establishment, idiomatically, means there is no charge.

clue.text: Get in harmony with writer beginning to strum hard

parts.note: the writer of a clue refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: the beginning of the word strum is its first letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A songwriter starts strumming hard to get in tune with the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears or ideas that fit together well engage, so to fit smoothly is to be in harmony.

clue.text: Attendant with the very best lock

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the very best, with the 1 read as the letter I
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A carer with the finest hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone serving food at tables is an attendant in a restaurant.

clue.text: Miss Penny once upon a time, born first

indicators.note: first says this piece goes in front of the other

parts.note: née marks a maiden name and means born
D was the abbreviation for the old British penny before decimal currency

explanation.surface: Miss Penny, born long ago, opens a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Penny' looks like a name; Miss is the verb, and D was the old British penny before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something is to feel the want of it, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: What keeps laciest pants up?

indicators.note: pants as a verb, to scramble about breathlessly, signals the letters of laciest rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what holds up some frilly knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is underwear in the surface but signals the anagram; the whole clue then defines the stretchy waistband material.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchy cord or band in a waistband is what holds underwear up.

clue.text: Oxford Uni fashion a wing that's isolated

parts.note: OU stands for Oxford University
the ton is an old word for fashionable society or fashion
a wing is a limb of a bird

explanation.surface: An Oxford college builds a new wing that stands alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like a verb meaning to build; it is the noun TON, as in 'the ton'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a precarious exposed position without support is an idiomatic sense of being isolated.

clue.text: Gridlock? I am on the way out

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
passé means old-fashioned, on the way out

explanation.surface: A driver stuck in a jam declares they are leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock where no progress is possible is a standstill, like traffic gridlock.

clue.text: Popular Bordeaux outside? Blow that!

indicators.note: outside means the wine wraps around the other piece

parts.note: claret is red wine from Bordeaux
in means popular

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a fashionable Bordeaux drunk outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow that!' sounds like an exclamation of annoyance; it means an instrument you blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument is played by blowing into it, so it is something to blow.

clue.text: One postgrad with manuscript for devotional officers

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MA, Master of Arts, is a postgraduate degree holder

explanation.surface: A postgraduate student hands in a manuscript about religious officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Muslim prayer leaders in a mosque are religious officials who lead worship.

clue.text: Subject to pressure I'll start to crumple

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
I'll is I will, and its I is used

indicators.note: the start of the word crumple is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone under pressure fears they are about to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to' looks like the definition phrase; only 'Subject' defines, and 'to' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme for discussion is a subject, a straightforward noun synonym.

clue.text: Carol, for instance, is thus … no good

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: A woman named Carol is judged to be no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name; it is a Christmas carol.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is one kind of musical piece sung aloud, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Turkey is among true quarry

indicators.note: is among puts the Turkey letters within the other word

parts.note: exact means true, accurate
TR is the international code for Turkey

explanation.surface: Turkey ranks among genuine targets of the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' looks like a noun, prey or a pit; it is the verb, to dig out.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarry stone is to dig it out of the ground, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Be responsible for ordinary poem having echo

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
a verse is a poem
Echo is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for E

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of a plain poem that repeats itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or manage something is to be in charge of it.

clue.text: Till old C&W singer is in wasted regret

parts.note: Johnny Cash was a country and western singer

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the rearranged letters
wasted means ruined or messed up, so the letters of regret are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran country singer wastes time in regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' looks like the word for 'until'; it is the shop drawer. Johnny Cash was a famous American country singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A till is the machine in a shop that records sales and holds the money.
